items.title: 'Noose is tightening': One Nation's new Victorian leader promoted conspiracy
items.description: The new state One Nation leader warned of a debunked "globalist" plot to control Australians.

items.title: 'National tragedy': Experts warn of concerning NAPLAN knowledge gaps
items.description: NAPLAN test scores have revealed one-third of Australian students are not meeting "challenging but reasonable" expectations in literacy and numeracy.

items.title: Police investigate arson on Victorian defence company as 'far-left terror'
items.description: It is the first time Australian authorities have investigated what they consider to be a potential far-left terror attack, motivated by anarchist and revolutionary ideology.

items.title: 'My brother has megarexia': Unregulated peptides exacerbating male eating disorders
items.description: Eating disorder dietician Alex Rodrigues said unregulated peptides being sold or shared in gym communities is a concerning trend in Australia.

items.title: 'Script hasn't changed': Kevin Rudd derides Hanson's leadership capability
items.description: Former prime minister Kevin Rudd says One Nation leader Pauline Hanson has no real answers for the issues facing Australians but he does believe AUKUS submarines are a good thing for the nation.

items.title: Tony Burke delays speech expected to reveal sweeping migration cuts
items.description: The ABC understands the cuts to migration numbers are contentious within Labor, but no reason for the delay is given.

items.title: Mass funeral held in Gaza for 112 people killed in Israeli strike
items.description: The group being laid to rest were members of two extended families in Gaza, with some gathered for the event describing it as the largest funeral in the war-ravaged strip's history.

items.title: These 10 Aussie wildflowers have superpowers. Pick your favourite
items.description: Move over waratahs and banksias! These 10 flowers from the unsung understorey are not just pretty faces, they have surprising tricks up their sleeves.

items.title: Big falls ahead for some of Australia's major stocks as they reveal profits
items.description: Australia's largest companies will reveal how they performed financially over the next few weeks, against the gloomy backdrop of a property downturn, stubborn inflation, higher interest rates and the Iran war.

items.title: A drifting part of a SpaceX rocket is about to crash into the Moon
items.description: Part of a SpaceX rocket will crash into the Moon, with the impact likely to be seen from Earth.

items.title: Five dead in Moscow region as Kyiv targets more Wildberries sites
items.description: Ukraine also targets another warehouse belonging to Russian e-commerce giant Wildberries as both sides trade strikes.

items.title: Solar costs for business to be slashed under energy scheme expansion
items.description: The federal government is set to announce changes to the Small-scale Renewable Energy scheme in a bid to help businesses install solar systems and close the gap with residential take-up.

items.title: Tasmanian child detained for 55 hours in adult watch house cell
items.description: Children have been detained in adult watch houses for up to 55 hours at a time, figures show, a year on since the Tasmanian government was urged to completely phase out the use of adult facilities for kids.

items.title: Nurses and midwives' union calls out 'gendered violence' after survey
items.description: Annalise has been kicked, punched and even bitten on the face while working as a nurse. Her experience is reflected in the Queensland Nurses and Midwives' Union's latest report into occupational violence in healthcare settings.

items.title: My Brilliant Career gets a reboot and a modern take
items.description: Netflix's six-episode adaptation of Miles Franklin's beloved novel features former Neighbours star Philippa Northeast as the firey protagonist.

items.title: What is parentification and how can you heal from it?
items.description: Eve was an adult when she realised she grew up in a home where the child-adult relationships were reversed.

items.title: Travel quiz: Will you pass with flying colours?
items.description: Where would you find the world's longest train tunnel? And how do you spell the name of the second-longest river in the US?

items.title: Sunny reprieve ahead for south-east Queensland as windy Ekka week looms
items.description: Forecasters say showery conditions are expected to ease across much of Queensland's east coast midway through this week.

items.title: 'Angry' grandmother torched home after being left out of will, court hears
items.description: A grandmother, who torched the home she'd lived in for decades after being left out of her late-husband's will, has been handed a suspended jail sentence.

items.title: Household spending increases in June, powered by EV sales
items.description: Australian household spending rose for a second month in June as consumers splashed out on electric vehicles amid rising fuel costs.

items.title: Labor unveils 'widow tax' fix after negative gearing backlash
items.description: The government is also consulting on carve-outs and changes covering newly built homes, affordable and disability housing and its new capital gains tax system.

items.title: Sportsbet, TAB deny allegations reps offered escort and drugs to gambler
items.description: Sportsbet and TAB have denied explosive claims they offered a young gambler access to illicit drugs and escorts as part of an inducement program.

items.title: US vow to dismantle the International Criminal Court labelled 'very worrying'
items.description: The Trump administration has vowed to dismantle the International Criminal Court "brick by brick", but analysts warn it's a move that has more to do with local politics than genuine concerns about the system.

items.title: More than 150 migrants saved from burning boat in English Channel
items.description: French coastguard officials have rescued migrants stranded on a burning boat in the English Channel.

items.title: Kath Pettingill, mother of accused Walsh Street police killers, dies
items.description: Kath Pettingill was the matriarch of the accused Melbourne crime family that was fictionalised in the 2010 movie Animal Kingdom.
